subject: MAP draft: technical evaluation milestones & proposed success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@nimbushealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft: technical evaluation milestones & proposed success criteria

Hi Sara / Raj —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand where Nimbus is on personalization and triage workflows. Per our call I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the technical evaluation milestone. The attachment contains milestone owners, dependencies, and a draft target close date.

Key asks for Nimbus to unblock Redwood running the technical benchmark:
- Provide a representative eval dataset (PII redacted) and expected query distribution by 9/3
- Confirm whether the evaluation will run in us-west or us-east (affects instance types)
- NDA/PO status (procurement contact cc'd) — need baseline PO/NDA before we provision dedicated test capacity

Proposed success criteria (high level):
- Semantic accuracy: average retrieval+response score >= 0.85 on the labeled eval set
- Hallucination: verified false-positives < 5% on critical queries
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for responses up to 128 tokens (approx)
- Cost: target per-response amortized cost <= $0.01 for production-config workload (options in bench template)

Model shortlist (we'll benchmark all candidates but recommend initial focus on):
- Llama-3-8B (quantized) — low-latency baseline
- Mistral-7B-Instruct — strong instruction-following at modest cost
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (server-side) — higher quality / fallback for edge cases

I've included a lightweight latency/throughput template (nimbus_latency_bench_template.xlsx) and the MAP draft PDF. Please review and confirm owners/target close date — I've put a suggested target close of 2026-09-30 in the draft to align with your Q4 rollout planning.

Next steps I propose:
1) Nimbus confirms dataset and region by 9/3
2) Redwood provisions test tenancy and runs first-pass benchmarks by 9/10
3) Joint readout and selection call w/ eng + security by 9/15

If that timeline looks tight for you, tell me which milestone needs to shift and we'll re-sequence. Happy to jump on 30-minute technical sync if helpful — Connor and Marissa are copied for availability.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: MAP draft: technical evaluation milestones & proposed success criteria

Ben —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the draft MAP. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock owners: 

1) Latency/cost targets: the p95 <= 300ms sounds reasonable but can you clarify whether that's measured from API gateway to first token or end-to-end generation for 128 tokens? For our clinical triage use case we care about end-to-end response time (including pre/post processing).

2) Model shortlist: we prefer open models but need to validate hallucination for clinical prompts. Would you be able to add a constrained hallucination test (we can share 50 clinical-critical prompts) and include hallucination-by-category in the output?

3) Security/data handling: We'll need to validate that test data is only used for benchmarking and not persisted in logs. Do you have a standard statement we can include in the MAP?

4) Timeline: Our clinical team is out the week of 9/6. If benchmarks need hands-on review we may need to push the joint readout to 9/20.

Attaching the procurement contact above — they'll confirm NDA/PO cadence. If you can answer Q1–Q3 we can assign owners on our side and confirm a firm target close date.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and I updated the MAP with two clarifying rows (see attached).

Q1 — latency definition: we measure end-to-end generation time from receipt of request at Redwood API to last-token-out for the configured response length (we can report both first-token latency and end-to-end). For the p95 <= 300ms target I meant end-to-end for responses up to 128 tokens. We'll provide both p95 and p99 in the benchmark report.

Q2 — hallucination tests: yes — please send the 50 clinical-critical prompts. We'll add a constrained hallucination suite and output hallucination-by-category (incorrect facts, invented references, medically unsafe suggestions). We'll return per-prompt labels and aggregated rates. Goal: medically unsafe suggestions < 1%, overall hallucination < 5%.

Q3 — data handling: Redwood will run benchmarks in a temporary test tenancy with logs disabled by default and KV/cache persisted only in ephemeral storage during the run. We'll include this statement in the MAP. If you need an explicit legal/data appendix we can append Redwood's standard bench-run handling clause.

Re: timeline: understood about 9/6 — propose we move the joint readout to 9/20 and shift final target close to 10/6 to allow time for security review. I've updated the MAP suggestion accordingly.

Owner suggestions (updated):
- Nimbus: provide eval dataset + label schema (owner: Sara) — due 2026-09-03
- Redwood (bench): run model sweep & bench report (owner: Connor) — first-pass 2026-09-12
- Nimbus (security): run review and confirm data-handling acceptance (owner: Raj) — due 2026-09-25
- Joint: readout + decision (owners: Sara / Ben) — 2026-09-20

Can Connor provision a short bench run (2 models, representative subset) once we have dataset access? Connor — are you good to take the bench owner role?

I'll standby for the 50 prompts and procurement update.

Best,
Ben

Sara / team —

Happy to take the bench owner role. Quick operational notes on how we'll run the technical evaluation so you know what to expect: 

1) Environment: we'll spin a temporary dedicated test tenancy scoped to Nimbus with VPC peering (or a redwood-managed isolated subnet) and explicit logs-disabled flag. Test runs are ephemeral and we'll share sanitized logs post-run.

2) Bench plan (first-pass):
- Phase A (smoke): run 500 representative queries across Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B-Instruct to validate pipeline and metric collection (2 business days)
- Phase B (full sweep): run 10k queries across shortlisted models including Falcon-40B-Instruct for high-quality baseline (4–6 business days)

3) Metrics we'll report (per-model):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (first-token and end-to-end)
- tokens/sec throughput at target concurrency
- amortized cost per 1k tokens at the run configuration
- semantic accuracy (normalized score against Nimbus labels) and top-line hallucination rate (by category)
- failure/error rate (timeouts, OOMs, retry counts)

4) Acceptance gate (proposed):
- semantic accuracy >= 0.85 AND hallucination rate < 5% AND p95 end-to-end <= 350ms for 128-token responses OR documented fallback plan showing acceptable cost/latency tradeoff.

5) Deliverables: bench report (spreadsheet + PDF readout), Dockerized inference config snippets, and a reproducible command list for Nimbus to re-run locally if desired.

Action items I have: confirm target concurrency and expected median response length (Sara) so I can size the test instances; request the 50 clinical-critical prompts; request dataset delivery method (S3 link or scp to provisioned host).

I can run Phase A as soon as we have dataset access — aiming to start 2026-09-07 if access is granted by 9/3. If the 9/7 start is blocked by team availability we can shift Phase A by a week.

I'll circle back with a short bench-run README and the commands we'll use so Nimbus can review before we run.
